name: Kingdom of Sweden (Gustavus Adolphus)

areaKm2.note: world_1600 Sweden polygons (13 features: Sweden proper, Finland, Estonia) = 679,396 km2 on the sphere. Livonia (conquered 1621-29) and Ingria/Kexholm (1617) are not in the 1600 polygon: add ~60,000-90,000 km2. Occupied Pomerania and Prussian ports excluded.

population.note: HYDE via OWID population.csv (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true): Sweden 766,244 (1600) and 1,368,171 (1700), interpolated ~0.96M for 1632; Finland 0.2M (1600) to 0.4M (1700), ~0.26M (other estimates ~0.35M); Estonia and Swedish Livonia ~0.15-0.25M. The Military Revolution article gives 1.1M for Sweden c. 1650. Occupied German territory excluded.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: Sweden 1.4% (1600), 4.0% (1700) (de Vries-type, Scandinavia). Stockholm ~10,000; Riga and Reval add Baltic towns. Mid 4% for the 5,000+ convention.

activePersonnel.note: Forces in Swedish pay in 1632: 140,000 in the Swedish intervention article infobox (25,000 Swedes and Finns in Germany, ~115,000 German allies and mercenaries), of which the Saxon and other allied armies (~25,000-40,000) are not Swedish; plus garrisons in Sweden, Finland and the Baltic (16,000 in Sweden and 6,500 for Finland in 1630, same article after Dodge). Mid ~100,000 Swedish-paid incl. navy. Parker (Military Revolution p. 24) gives 45,000 for the national army of the 1630s (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Revolution); 149,000 is the Nov 1632 paper total often quoted.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: next utskrivning levy class and the lantvarn (home defence levy) callable within a month.

supportPersonnel.note: Navy ~5,000-7,000 sailors (Glete, Navies and Nations: ~30 major warships), artillery corps and train ~3,000-5,000 (regimental guns with every infantry regiment), commissariat ~1,000.

mobilizationRatio.note: Includes the mercenary market Sweden bought with French subsidies and German contributions (Barwalde 1631): Swedish-paid strength of 100,000-150,000 was 7-11% of the home population. The native-only ceiling was ~4-5% (the utskrivning drafted ~50,000 Swedes and Finns 1621-32; Frost, Northern Wars ch. 6, isbn:0-582-06429-5).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Swedish, Finnish, Scottish and German infantry brigades (pike and musket in ~1:2 ratio). Share of the Swedish-paid total after subtracting cavalry (~25-30%); grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical) to 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: lightened musket, cartridges, regimental 3-pdrs; the leading tactical system of 1630-32

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: drilled native brigades 0.85, German recruits after 1631 0.6

count.note: Cuirassier and harquebusier regiments charging home with the sword (Swedish and German), ~1/4 of cavalry as heavy.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: charge-oriented Swedish horse supported by commanded musketeers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: veteran of the Prussian war 1626-29

count.note: Finnish (hakkapeliitta), Swedish and German horse regiments of medium-light type and dragoons.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: small Nordic horses, pistols and swords

count.note: Educated guess: two light regimental guns per infantry regiment plus field and siege trains; Breitenfeld 1631 saw ~75 Swedish guns with the main army.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: light leather and 3-pdr regimental guns, standardised calibres under Torstensson: the era's most mobile field artillery

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Torstensson's artillery regiment

count.note: Glete, Navies and Nations (1993) tables: Swedish navy c. 1630-35 ~30 major warships (~20,000-25,000 tons). Vasa (1628) sank on launch. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mixed new-built ships; Baltic-sized warships

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: Baltic sea control against Poland, no major fleet battle

count.note: Educated guess: smaller warships, pinnaces and transports in naval service.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: conscripted seamen

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 1.0 (best-in-era). Evidence: Gustavus Adolphus (Breitenfeld 1631, Lech 1632), Banér, Torstensson, Horn; killed at Lutzen 16 Nov 1632

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: native brigades with strong identity; growing mercenary share after 1631 lowered cohesion

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Protestant cause and unbroken victories 1630-32

weapons.note: Anchor: 5 (1600) toward 6. Evidence: Swedish brigade, lighter musket, paper cartridges, regimental guns: the most advanced tactical system of 1632 audit 2026-10-30: mid 5.25 -> 5.16, capped at the SOURCES.md tech anchor interpolated for 1632 (5.156); the mid may not exceed the anchor for its year.

armor.note: Anchor: 5 (half-armor, cuirass). Evidence: cuirassiers and armoured pikemen

fortification.note: Anchor: 5 (trace italienne). Evidence: bastioned works at Riga, Stralsund and Baltic ports

logistics.note: Anchor: 5 (magazines). Evidence: contributions system and Baltic sea transport; Swedish-paid armies largely lived off German territory

communications.note: Anchor: 4.9. Evidence: courier network; Oxenstierna administered from Prussia and the Rhine

isr.note: Anchor: ISR uses the same years as the anchor table (1600 -> 5, 1805 -> 6). Evidence: cavalry screens, spies and merchant reports only; no aerial or signal intelligence

air.note: No aircraft or military balloons before 1783/1794.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (2011 int$): Sweden 1630 = 1,423, 1632 = 1,605, 1640 = 1,701; Finland 1600/1650 = 1,191/1,246. Mid 1,500 weights Finland and the Baltic provinces in.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: home revenue (copper, Prussian tolls, taxes) of ~3M riksdaler could not fund the war; French subsidies (400,000 rdr a year from 1631) and German contributions paid most of it. Peacetime share lower.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: copper (Falun the largest European source) and iron exports, gun founding (Finspang); agrarian economy.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: thin northern agriculture, Baltic grain (Livonia, Prussian ports) supplemented supply.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.009-0.011 (mid 0.0095): in a pre-transition age structure (Wrigley and Schofield type, life expectancy ~30-35) males reaching 18 each year are about 0.9-1.1% of total population. Males only.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: tracks between Swedish market towns; winter sledge routes; Baltic sea lanes carried most traffic.

majorPorts.note: Stockholm, Kalmar, Gothenburg (founded 1621), Riga, Reval, Turku, Stralsund (allied 1628), plus occupied Prussian ports.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: small domestic shipping; copper and iron largely carried by Dutch ships.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-54657-5) ch. 1: 17th-18th c. armies tied to magazines and bread ovens, operating ~5 marches (~100-150 km) beyond the nearest magazine or navigable river; requisition extends it in rich country. Swedish armies relied on contributions in Germany and the Oder, Elbe and Main rivers. audit 2026-10-30: grade C -> D: cited by ISBN only, with no fetched copy of the book (SOURCES.md grading rule).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses and oxen for 1.35M people; cavalry remounts bought in Germany.

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: deep strategic depth, forest and lakes, harsh winters, sea moat; invasion of Sweden proper rarely attempted.

notes: Snapshot = 1632, Gustavus Adolphus in Germany (Alte Veste, Lutzen). Population counts Sweden proper, Finland, Estonia, Livonia and Ingria; occupied German lands excluded. Personnel convention: all regiments in Swedish pay (native conscripts and German/Scottish mercenaries) are active because they were salaried and under arms; allied armies (Saxony, Brandenburg, Hesse) are excluded; the next levy and the lantvarn are trainedReserves. This makes active larger than a native mobilization ratio would allow, so mobilizationRatio includes the subsidised mercenary market (stated there). The 140,000-150,000 headline totals are paper strengths mixing Swedish-paid and allied forces.
